overview: This file documents the April–May 1948 liberalization of international postal service to and from occupied Japan. A despatch from the United States Political Adviser in Tokyo forwards SCAP Instruction 1884 and an accompanying press release to the Department of State. The instruction authorizes books, magazines, and other printed matter to enter international mails under the Universal Postal Union Convention, while the press release presents the expansion as part of Japan’s gradual restoration of prewar communications and as a means of encouraging commercial, scientific, artistic, and cultural exchange.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 268 forwarding materials on international mail service
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards SCAP’s new instruction and press release liberalizing the rules governing international printed matter mailed to and from Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Political Adviser forwards five copies each of SCAPIN 1884 and a related headquarters press release. The instruction, issued on April 25, 1948, expands international postal privileges to include books, magazines, and other printed matter. The despatch identifies both items as enclosures and records that the original and an ozalid copy were sent to the Department of State.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1884 on international mail service
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; signed by R. H. Levy for the Supreme Commander
subfiles.about: The memorandum authorizes international mailing of printed matter to and from Japan beginning May 1, 1948.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 1884 amends three earlier SCAP memoranda governing international mail service. Effective May 1, 1948, it authorizes books, magazines, and all other matter classified as “Prints,” subject to the Universal Postal Union Convention adopted at Buenos Aires in 1939. It also permits direct technical communication between SCAP staff sections and the Japanese Ministry of Communications.

subfiles.title: Press release announcing expansion of Japan’s international postal service
subfiles.from: Public Information Office, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.about: The press release announces worldwide international-mail eligibility for printed matter to and from Japan and explains its practical and cultural significance.
subfiles.summary: SCAP announces that all mailable matter classified as “Prints” may be sent between Japan and every country beginning May 1, 1948. The release places the measure within the gradual expansion of international mail since limited service resumed on September 10, 1946. It emphasizes international mail’s value for commerce, industry, science, art, culture, and the freer flow of information, and gives a detailed list of qualifying printed materials and production processes.

interest: The file offers a compact view of how an occupation directive moved from administrative order to diplomatic reporting and public presentation. It is especially useful for studying the restoration of Japan’s postwar links with the outside world and SCAP’s portrayal of freer information exchange as essential to democratization, culture, and economic recovery. The unusually detailed definition of “printed matter” also provides evidence about the technologies, media, and postal classifications recognized in 1948.
